findings.title: Compilation error: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` called without required `UserModel` argument
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes compilation to fail; `context.getUser()` needs to be passed (or an overload provided).

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `false` when `user` is `null`, breaking initial passkey login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During normal initial login (before a user is identified in the authentication context) and on error challenges where the user is cleared, `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and challenges are not added to the login form on initial login. Conversely, when `user != null` (such as during re-authentication), it does not check whether the user actually has a passkey credential configured (e.g., `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`), so passkey UI will be enabled and `UsernameForm` will not be skipped even for users without passkeys.
